newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels seize Kindu town, airport-U.N. source.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels seize Kindu town, airport-U.N. source.

text.p: Rebels have seized the eastern Zairean town of Kindu and its airport and agencies ordered the evacuation of foreign aid workers from Tingi Tingi refugee camp, a U.N. source said on Friday.
"It is confirmed that Kindu and its airport fell to the rebels yesterday (on Thursday)," said a U.N. source who declined to be identified.
"An immediate evacuation of all expatriates from Tingi Tingi is being ordered as camp leaders have warned that the camp will be attacked tonight," said the source, who had no more details.

A regional military source said on Thursday morale among government troops in Kindu was low and panic had set in among them. But he said the rebels were holding off to allow as many civilians to leave as possible.
Kindu, a key, heavily fortified transport hub on the Zaire River, had the northernmost working station on a rail line to South Africa. It also had a large airport used by the military.
Tingi Tingi, to the northeast of Kindu, has some 170,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees who fled earlier rebel advances.
